messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SLO breach detected for streaming p99 latency on model redwood-llm-int8-v2 in prod-eu. p99 > 3.0s for the last 5m, error rate steady. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

oncall-ryan: Acked. I'm on it — pulling metrics now. Seeing p99 spikes up to 6-8s on streaming responses, p95 around 1.2s. Throughput unchanged. Queues per runtime shard climbing (~200 -> 650).

eng-ml-sam: I rolled a new int8 calibration profile ~2h ago (autocalib job completed). Quick hypothesis: quant calibration changed KV cache behavior and increased dequant overhead for long contexts. Also saw a bump in attention kernel time in telemetry.

eng-runtime-lee: Confirming logs from the serving runtime: a subset of replicas show repeated `KV_CACHE_MISS` followed by `DEQUANT_CALL` spikes. Example trace:```
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] shard-7 GET /stream token=... latency=7564ms events=[KV_CACHE_MISS, DEQUANT_CALL, ATTENTION_RECOMPUTE]
```

sre-anya: Is this isolated to eu region or global?

eng-ml-sam: Mostly eu. Canary in us-east shows no change. Calibration rollout targeted eu pool.

support-jess: Support: We're already seeing ~12 customer incidents in last 30m. 3 customers flagged as P1 (high traffic apps). CS note: customers reporting stalled streaming (client shows "waiting for tokens").

oncall-ryan: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic away from redwood-llm-int8-v2 to fp16 variant for streaming routes, 2) scale up dedicated pool shards for eu, 3) pause int8 auto-calib job. I'll start 1 and 3 now.

eng-runtime-lee: To divert: `routectl set-weight --route streaming.modelX --model redwood-llm-fp16-v3 --weight 1.0` should swap over. Will execute in 2m and watch backlog.

eng-ml-sam: I'll disable the calibration job on the scheduler: `cronscheduler disable autocalib-eu-int8` and revert the calibration artifact if needed. The previous calibration hash is `calib-20260314-a1`.

incident-bot: Action logged: oncall-ryan moved streaming traffic to redwood-llm-fp16-v3 at 2026-03-15T20:18:12Z.

oncall-ryan: Traffic moved. Observability: p99 for streaming dropped to 1.1s within 3m, queues cleared from 650 -> 100. Starting to message affected customers.

support-jess: Update sent to customers. Interim mitigation: routing to fp16. Customers asked to expect degraded cost (higher compute) but restored latency.

customer-ops-bob: Flagging contract impact for 3 P1s — will coordinate credits if prolonged. Logging for legal review.

eng-runtime-lee: We should capture full telemetry for the impacted replicas before we tear them down. Snapshotting logs/kv cache metrics now. Command: `servingctl snapshot --shard shard-7 --out /tmp/snap-5198765432.tar.gz`

eng-ml-sam: Collected model calibration diff: `diff calib-20260314-a1 calib-20260315-b2` shows changed scale factors on several layers and a new per-head quant table. I'm attaching the snippet here:```
-layer_7.scale: 0.0078 -> 0.0052
-head_2.quant_bias: 0.00012 -> 0.00045
```
These changes could increase dequant jitter for long contexts. Need offline eval to confirm.

sre-anya: Next steps for post-incident: - full rollback or rework calibration? - add canary gating for auto-calib with tail-latency monitors.

oncall-ryan: For now we won't rollback customer-facing code beyond routing. eng-ml, please prepare a rollback plan for the calibration (re-apply previous calib hash) and a staged canary with tail-latency watch.

eng-ml-sam: Will prepare rollback. Proposed rollout: 1) reapply calib-20260314-a1 to a 10% canary in eu, 2) monitor p99 streaming for 15m, 3) if stable, ramp. Also adding a replay test that simulates long streaming contexts.

eng-runtime-lee: I'll open a hotpatch to add a short-circuit fallback: if `DEQUANT_CALL` > 2x baseline in 1m, route that shard's traffic away automatically. Patch ready to deploy.

incident-bot: Paging: oncall handoff scheduled in 60m.

oncall-ryan: Handoff summary for next oncall (eng-runtime-lee): cause likely int8 calibration change in eu causing increased dequant/attention recompute and KV cache pressure -> streaming stalls and p99 spike. Mitigation done: traffic routed to fp16, autocalib paused, snapshots taken. Customer impact: ~12 affected, 3 P1s. Action items assigned to eng-ml-sam (rollback plan + offline eval), eng-runtime-lee (hotpatch gating + snapshot analysis), sre-anya (postmortem + SLO impact report), support-jess (customer comms).

eng-runtime-lee: Acked. I'll take watch and start immediate hotpatch and telemetry drill. If we see recurrence after re-enabling calib, I'll trigger full rollback.

support-jess: Noted. I'll update the customer thread with mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

sre-anya: I'll start the incident doc: `incidents/5198765432-calib-latency-surge` and include timelines/graphs. Requesting timestamped metric exports from observability (20:00-20:30 UTC).

eng-ml-sam: One more item — we should add a regression test to the autocalib pipeline that runs a small streaming tail-latency synthetic load for 1k examples to catch this kind of variance. Adding to backlog and prioritizing as bug.

oncall-ryan: Thanks team. Leaving handoff note and will be reachable if needed.

eng-runtime-lee: Hotpatch deployed to gating in 2m. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (traffic diverted). Oncall handoff in progress. Postmortem required.

sre-anya: Filing postmortem checklist now. Will assign follow-ups for canary gating, autocalib rollback safeguards, customer credits estimation, and telemetry alerts for KV_CACHE_MISS spikes.

support-jess: Closing customer loop after patch verification.

eng-ml-sam: I'll attach calibration diffs and offline eval results to the incident doc once available.
